subject: Traffic simulation booking & capacity commitment
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@zephyr.ai>, Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — Traffic simulation windows + next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan.

Summary from today
- Objective: validate Zephyr’s peak QPS (35k ephemeral QPS observed during peak) and confirm Redwood Dedicated sizing and test window to validate latency SLOs under 95th pct load.
- Success criteria: 95th latency < 350ms for user-facing endpoint; no more than 5% request errors at peak.

Proposed test plan (high level)
1) Traffic simulation (prefix + randomized user traces) — 3-hour window at 1.25x reported peak (target: 43,750 QPS) to exercise headroom and KV cache behavior.
2) Focused stress ramp — 30m ramps to 2x (70k) to validate graceful degradation and fallback routing.
3) Post-run: token/sample-level traces and consolidated perf report within 48h.

Milestones & owners (draft MAP items)
- Schedule test window (owner: Zephyr, contact: Sarah) — propose 2 candidate windows in the next 2 weeks.
- Redwood capacity estimate and runbook (owner: Redwood SE) — action: Karthik to produce sizing and detailed runbook.
- Access & accounts (owner: Zephyr) — provide test keys and list of endpoints; Ethan to confirm network egress rules.
- Final sign-off and target close of MAP milestone: aim to complete testing and sign capacity/commit by 2026-08-15.

Dependencies
- Dedicated capacity availability and model variant (quantization profile) selection.
- Test data export and traffic anonymization confirmation from Zephyr.

Immediate asks
- Sarah/Ethan: please confirm two candidate windows (dates + start times) by end of day tomorrow so we can lock capacity. I attached a simple CSV with example windows.
- Karthik/Marissa: please draft a quick capacity sketch and rough estimate (GPU count / instance shapes) by EOD Wednesday.

Attachments: traffic-sim-windows.csv (proposed slots)

Thanks — I’ll update the MAP doc after we pick a window.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

From: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@zephyr.ai>

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Traffic simulation windows + next steps

Thanks Rachel — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed peak: 35k sustained QPS for ~20 minutes during business-critical flows; bursty sections up to ~60k for <5m.
- We can provide anonymized traces and a sanitized request corpus (S3 link) — will share via secure bucket.
- Candidate windows (all PDT):
  * Option A: Tue 2026-07-28 02:00–05:00 PDT
  * Option B: Thu 2026-07-30 00:00–03:00 PDT

On capacity: we want Redwood to propose Dedicated sizing that meets the success criteria. If possible, include a lower-cost config to try first (smaller cluster) and a recommended committed configuration.

We’ll also need a short statement for procurement that lays out the required minimum capacity and the expected burn during the stress run. Can Redwood provide that?

Attaching: traffic-corpus-s3-link.txt

Sarah Gomez
VP of Product Operations, Zephyr Analytics

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 12:40:00 -07:00

Forwarding Sarah’s confirmation — they picked two windows. Need a quick sizing + procurement blurb.

Ask for Karthik / Marissa
- Karthik: draft the capacity estimate (rough GPU count, expected token/sec, whether 8xA100 equiv or 12xA10x is recommended) + runbook bullets (KV cache priming, prefix caching settings, batch size limits). Include an estimated cost range and a one-paragraph procurement note that Sarah can pass to finance.
- Marissa: flag any operational dependencies (observability hooks, tracing URLs, temporary quota increases) and confirm whether we can support the proposed windows on our Dedicated pool without impacting other reserved customers.

Target: please send drafts by EOD today so Rachel can push back to Zephyr and lock the window (they asked to confirm by EOD tomorrow).

Thanks — R.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@zephyr.ai>, Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@zephyr.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Traffic simulation windows + next steps

Thanks — rough sizing notes below (quick turn for procurement). I’ll follow up with an XLS with line-item cost and runbook steps.

Quick capacity sketch (targets aligned to success criteria)
- Baseline test (1.25x sustained peak = 43,750 QPS) — recommended: 6 x A100-80GB equiv (or 9 x A10x-48GB equiv) in a dedicated pool. This config provides steady-state throughput and room for KV cache overhead.
- Stress ramp (2x burst test = 70k QPS) — require short-term burst capacity: either temporary 2x burst nodes or throttled rate limiter; if Zephyr wants continuous 2x runs, move to 10 x A100 equiv.
- Memory and KV cache notes: large-context models require preserving KV cache; allocate 200GB aggregate GPU memory across the pool to keep latency low.

Procurement blurb (one paragraph)
"Redwood Inference recommends reserving a temporary dedicated GPU pool to validate performance at your observed peak traffic. For the initial validation run (target 1.25x sustained peak), we estimate 6 x NVIDIA A100-class GPUs (or equivalent instances) and a short burst policy to 8–10 GPUs for stress ramps. Cost for a single three-hour validation window, including telemetry and post-run analysis, is estimated in the attached spreadsheet. Completing this milestone enables Zephyr to finalize committed capacity recommendations and validate latency SLOs before signing a production commitment."

Milestone owners & target dates (updated)
- Zephyr: pick final window and share test keys — ETA: 2026-07-24 (Sarah)
- Redwood SE (Karthik): capacity estimate + runbook + procurement blurb — ETA: 2026-07-23 (today) — attached: capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx
- Redwood Ops (Marissa): verify pool availability & temp quota — ETA: 2026-07-24
- MAP milestone target: testing complete and recommendation ready — 2026-08-15

Attachments: capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx

I’ll also add a short note in the MAP doc with dependencies: model variant, quantization profile, and whether Zephyr wants prefix caching enabled for production parity.

Karthik
